messages:
alex: restore-monitor alerted: restore job 4482 failed while pulling snapshot from archival-bucket-3.
alex: error in logs -> 
```
ERROR: decrypt_snapshot: missing envelope metadata header 'x-rw-envelope-id' for object s3://archival-bucket-3/snapshots/2026-03-16/tenant-77.snap
CausedBy: metadata header not found, cannot locate envelope key id
```
priya: yikes. that header is what we store at object-level so we can look up the envelope key and call KMS to unwrap. if it's missing the object seems opaque. any recent changes to replication or copy jobs?
matt: we rolled a new cross-region replication proxy last week (replicator-v2) that uses a managed copy lambda. vendor docs: default S3-compatible copy can drop custom user metadata unless you specify metadata-copy. i asked infra to add it but not sure it landed.
jordan: also changed the replicator service account on 03/14 to use the new short-lived-role (repl-role-prod) to comply with least-priv. might've been a permission scoping mistake.
priya: good catch. if the copy used metadata-directive=REPLACE without reattaching user metadata, that would strip x-rw-* headers while keeping object data and storage-class.
gloria: severity? are any customer restores impacted or was it internal staging?
alex: the monitor is for both staging and prod restores. so far detected failures for 12 restore attempts in the last 2 hours across 4 tenants. none appear to have succeeded. no evidence of plaintext data exposure.
sam_bot: audit-log: https://internal.logs/redwood/search?q=replicator-v2%20metadata-directive returned entries showing copy_object calls at 1765960000-1766000000. Attached: action=CopyObject, source=archival-bucket-2, dest=archival-bucket-3, metadataDirective=REPLACE, userMetadata={}.
matt: that matches. metadataDirective=REPLACE was set in the wrapper lambda to sanitize metadata to avoid leaking internal tags. forgot that we rely on userMetadata for envelope ids. my bad.
jordan: KMS side: even if header existed, replication should not require decrypt. we persist envelope id and encrypted key in metadata. removing that breaks ability to locate the envelope in our key registry.
priya: mitigation steps I'm proposing: 1) run a backward scan to find objects where x-rw-envelope-id missing but object size and prefix look like snapshots; 2) attempt to reconstruct envelope id from manifest files (if any) in the same prefix; 3) where not possible, re-encrypt object by generating a new envelope and calling KMS to rewrap — but that requires us to trust that object is unchanged and was never exposed; 4) fix replicator to copy metadata and redeploy.
gloria: add: update runbook and notify affected customers if restores were blocked. need timeline and pager for follow ups.
matt: immediate fix: change metadataDirective to COPY and redeploy replicator-v2. I can patch and roll in the next 10m.
jordan: we should also tighten IAM on repl-role-prod to allow s3:GetObjectTagging and s3:GetObjectVersion (if applicable) and ensure it has kms:GenerateDataKey/Decrypt only for the envelope keys repo lookup flow. but don't grant broad kms:Decrypt.
alex: running quick query now to enumerate affected prefixes: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket archival-bucket-3 --prefix snapshots/2026-03- --query "Contents[?contains(Key, 'tenant')].Key"` then check head-object for metadata.
sam_bot: scan started, report will be at https://internal.tasks/scan/scan-7821 in ~9m.
priya: let's contain blast: temporarily disable replicator-v2 copy for new snapshot uploads (fail open or queue instead) so we don't create more stripped objects. matt -> can you flip to queue mode?
matt: yes, switching to queue mode now, will confirm when done.
alex: decided incident severity P2 for now. no confirmed data leakage, but restore reliability is impacted.
gloria: assign owners: matt (replicator rollback/patch), priya (restore triage + reconstruct plan), jordan (KMS & IAM scoping), alex (detection + customer impact). I'll own comms if we need to alert customers.
priya: triage note: look for manifests under `snapshots/2026-03-16/*.manifest` sometimes we persist envelope ids there; if present we can batch reattach metadata using `s3.copy_object` with metadataDirective=REPLACE and set userMetadata back. safer than re-encrypting.
janet (from support): heads-up — we already have 2 support tickets flagged as "restore error: cannot decrypt snapshot". I'll hold on notifying customers until we know scope.
gloria: timeline: patch replicator in 15m, full scan results in 10m, initial remediation runbook decision in 30m, postmortem doc afterwards. Make sure to capture who approved metadata copy change and why sanitization landed.
matt: patch applied and replicator queued. tests show metadata now preserved on new copies.
sam_bot: scan report: 23 objects missing x-rw-envelope-id in archival-bucket-3/snapshots/2026-03-16; 17 have matching manifest files; 6 have no manifest.
priya: plan: restore metadata for the 17 via copy_object to add userMetadata from manifest -> re-run decrypt. for 6 without manifest, escalate to legal+security for guidance before re-encrypting or reprocessing.
jordan: we'll add an additional immutable audit header `x-rw-seal` in the future that's copied by the proxy unchanged — helps detection if metadata was stripped.
gloria: good. postmortem owners: priya to draft initial incident summary, add timeline, root cause = replicator sanitization + insufficient test coverage for metadata preservation, action items include IAM scoping review, stronger pre-deploy tests, and one-click replay tool.
alex: thanks team — if anyone finds any restored plaintext or suspicious accesses, tag me and @oncall. we'll regroup in 45m for status. :thumbsup:
